scope: manual semantic and visual review of one region's eight generated A5 source masters before deterministic compile
review_unit: one 384x384 source master plus 48x48 normalized preview

required_checks_per_source.requirement: The image clearly reads as the material named by its stable source ID and does not substitute a different surface family.
The image is a continuous top-down material surface, not a landscape, room, prop illustration, sprite, icon, object pile, map, UI panel or perspective scene.
No visible tile grid, checkerboard, atlas layout, contact-sheet framing, cell borders or repeated panel arrangement.
No text, letters, numbers, pseudo-text, glyphs, signs, logos, runes, emblems or symbolic markings.
No isolated props, furniture, plants, tools, debris clusters or landmarks that would make deterministic wrapped variants look like duplicated objects.
Large-scale lighting and feature distribution are reasonably even enough for wrap-offset extraction; no dominant edge-to-edge directional composition or obvious framing.
The surface retains subtle handcrafted Plushtopia/Plushbound material character without becoming fuzzy toy fabric or decorative textile print unless that material specifically requires woven matting.
The material belongs plausibly to the target region's established environmental language without modern-world contamination.

required_region_checks.requirement: All eight accepted sources are visually distinct enough to supply separate material families.
The set reads as one target region and does not import signature identity from another region.
No two source masters are duplicate or near-duplicate renders masquerading as separate materials.
The eight-source contact sheet is coherent as a regional A5 palette while preserving material differentiation.

pass_rule: PASS_8_OF_8 only when every per-source check passes for all eight sources and every region-level check passes.
failure_rule: Any failing source quarantines that source/region for targeted review; passing source IDs remain protected from rerender. A failure never authorizes catalog-wide regeneration.
